meta.title: 170: My ADHD son tells all!!!
meta.description:
I asked my son to do something that at this point shouldn’t be a battle at all. But it was. I asked my son to brush his teeth before bed. I know I know, what a terrible mom! As soon as I asked, his refusal kicked on, his silliness increased, he was delaying, delaying, delaying. 

I was able to talk to him after the power struggle and in fact audio recorded so I could hear him and learn what was getting in his way. 

HE SPILLED THE MOST IMPORTANT DETAILS! And I’m sharing them with you!! Get ready to understand your kids like never before! I am breaking down each sentence and the peer reviewed studies that back up everything he is saying!!! It’s wild and so so important to know!


🚨FIRST EVER ADHD BEHAVIOR BLUEPRINT 🚨LIVE EVENT IS HAPPENING!!🚨

You’re having the same power struggle over the tasks that HAVE to get done. Homework, teeth brushing, putting ONE piece of clothing away, bedtime… heaven forbid you ALSO ask that they speak kindly during this process. 🤯

The level of overwhelm, dysregulation, and frustration you’re living with day to day is real and it’s unfair. 🙅🏼‍♀️This is NOT what you pictured parenting to look like, and this version of you as a parent, is not aligning with your values. 

You want to be a kind, accepting, patient person but you end up snapping or getting into your ADHD kid’s feelings with them.

🎉But that all changes now! 🎉

You’re going to be able to stop walking on eggshells, stop feeling utterly defeated and like you’re making all the wrong choices, and ACTUALLY KNOW how you and your child can get through both transitions and all the everyday “must do tasks” without yet another fight! AND, you don’t need to repeat yourself to the point of yelling!

Imagine feeling grounded and proud of yourself for navigating the day with regulation instead of multiple yelling matches. 

There are many ADHD strategies out there, but after working exclusively with severe high conflict families, I’ve filtered out what doesn’t work for ADHD kids (*cough gentle parenting) and combined my education, research & lived experience into the core A.B.L.E. Method. 

You do not need to have the same battle every day. It starts with regulation, a plan, some practice reps, and a lot of reinforcement. Not sure how that looks in real life? Don’t worry! I’ve got your back in a 2 day live event (well on zoom but with me😂) where we go over YOUR repeated battle and we BUILD YOUR PLAN so all you have to do is execute it!

January 9th & 10th, 2027 (9am-11am PST both days) *Recorded for those who can’t attend live. 

No more second guessing, no more confusion, just a proven strategy to support your power struggle. 

This live event IS FREE to all existing ResponseABLE Community members! 

So come to a free masterclass or just JOIN THE PROGRAM, and get ready to have me walk side by side with you as we map out your 2027 behavior plan so you can actually start enjoying time with your ADHD child again! 

FREE masterclass: https://calendly.com/responseableparenting/adhd-masterclass

JOIN here: https://www.responseableparenting.com/join 

Live event dates: Jan 9-10th. 2 hours on Saturday / 2 hours on Sunday morning (9-11am PST).  We take your chronic fight and your goal and we break down every step that needs to happen to make that goal a reality! 

MINI COURSE:

Grab my 39 minute video / workbook combo where you will learn exactly why you feel so awful in these moments with your ADHD kid AND you’ll learn the steps necessary to get out of the heat of the moment and stop reacting so quickly to the same repetitive fight. 

You can grab Before You Lose It right here! https://responseable-community.circle.so/checkout/gap 

FREE RESOURCES!

Tired of repeating yourself over the same behaviors? Try this VALUES DECK OF CARDS! You can customize the cards to your family values and instead of dishing out yet another punishment, you can instill positive consequences through the actions on the back!
https://responseableparenting.kit.com/cards

Get the cheat codes to “stack” regulation practices throughout your day! No time to meditate? No problem. Grab this simple system and add ZERO time to your day!
https://responseableparenting.kit.com/zero

Book a call with me to connect on areas of your parenting that are causing pain, struggle, or frustration. https://calendly.com/responseableparenting/call

summary.one_liner: A parenting coach shares her ADHD son's own description of what happens in his brain and body during meltdowns, matched to peer-reviewed research.
summary.summary:
Becky Jennings recounts a bedtime conflict with her ADHD son that turned into a surprisingly candid conversation about what he experiences when asked to do non-preferred tasks. He describes feeling controlled by "energy," experiencing refusal requests as literal electric shocks, and having his thoughts go "pitch black" when overwhelmed. Jennings connects each of his descriptions to specific studies on dopamine, delay aversion, amygdala reactivity, working memory, and inner speech development in ADHD children.

The core insight is that non-preferred tasks are processed by the ADHD brain as a physical threat, which fires the amygdala, knocks the prefrontal cortex offline, and shuts down the inner voice that would normally help a child self-correct in the moment. This explains why logic and reasoning don't work during a meltdown, and why yelling sometimes becomes the only "spark" intense enough to get a frozen child moving.

Her son also revealed that he never misbehaves at school because he gets frequent built-in rewards (recess, lunch, positive teacher feedback), while home interactions skew more corrective. Jennings uses this to argue parents need to build in choice, quick wins, breaks, and praise rather than relying on anger to motivate action, and she ties this into promotion for her coaching program's masterclass and a January two-day planning event.
takeaways: ADHD kids often experience requests to do non-preferred tasks as a physical threat, not just an annoyance.
Dopamine in ADHD brains tends to get stuck on the reward itself rather than linking it to the task needed to earn it, making delayed rewards feel nearly worthless.
Waiting and boredom activate the amygdala and insula in ADHD brains, producing a real felt sense of discomfort rather than mere impatience.
When the amygdala fires, the prefrontal cortex goes offline, taking logic, working memory, and communication with it, which is why reasoning doesn't work mid-meltdown.
The self-guided inner voice that helps most people adjust their behavior develops later in ADHD kids, so external narration from parents can help fill that gap.
Kids with ADHD often know what they want to do and even want to cooperate, but struggle with follow-through due to these brain-based barriers.
Yelling can inadvertently work as an arousal spike that activates an under-aroused ADHD brain, which is why kids may wait for it before acting.
Immediate, frequent small rewards and praise (like what often happens at school) are more effective motivators for ADHD kids than delayed consequences.
Building practice, play, novelty, and built-in breaks into routines can replace yelling as the spark needed to start tasks.
